parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, facility ban, border targeting or custody exposure is documented, and same-sex conduct is legal. National anti-discrimination law covering goods/services since 2015 and hate-crime penalties provide paper recourse, with a court ruling permitting marker change without surgery and visible capital Pride/legal-aid infrastructure as climate signals. Offsetting this, implementation is reported inconsistent, reporting to police is low, politicians' hate speech and threats around Pride are documented, and border, facilities, custody and visitor-care practices are not documented. Under the rubric this is documented acceptance with imperfectly proven remedies, not operational protection at the 0.85 level.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No source on border, airport screening, or treatment of foreign documents/markers for visitors.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No source on police custody, detention placement or verification exams for trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Constitutional equality and hate-crime provisions are general recourse signals only.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward, shelter or sex-segregated facility rule for visitors is stated.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers goods/services, housing, education since 2015, but visitor facility application is not documented.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for short-term visitors; hormone continuity and emergency care not addressed.
care_services.protection: Resident services include trans support for hormonal procedures via ministry cooperation and free HIV/PrEP at national clinic since June 2024; not documented as visitor access.
care_services.interaction: Resident care does not establish traveller-facing care access.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Political hate speech common in civil-code debates, intolerance reported, death threats to artist, anonymous threats around Pride. No trans-specific presentation offence documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2019 criminal code adds penalties for gender-identity hate crimes; official calling for beheadings was taken into custody.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile political speech coexists with formal hate-crime penalties and arrests for extreme speech.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No age-specific visitor, schooling, care or custody rule for trans minors or guardians is stated.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2019: 10 bias crimes reported to authorities, 13 only to LGBTQ organisations; tendency not to report. No trans-specific violence rate with denominator; 2015 LGBTQ-wide survey is dated and not trans-specific.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Free confidential legal aid and psychological support via capital LGBTQI+ organisation; hate-crime penalties exist.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Low police reporting suggests recourse is underused despite formal penalties.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Implementation of anti-discrimination framework reported inconsistent (March 2026); court marker-change precedent refused as precedent, each applicant must litigate — resident-facing, not visitor exposure.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid organisation, courts, constitutional equality provide potential remedies, efficacy for visitors not documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns on border, facilities, custody and visitor care prevent crediting unproven protections.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in having formal equality protections with inconsistent frontline application and occasional friction, with remedies not shown to be prompt. This case is higher because no brief detention or document-mismatch hold is documented, but lower certainty follows from undocumented visitor practices.

Similar in having anti-discrimination and hate-crime recourse with discretionary, uneven enforcement. This case lacks documented border training, tribunal remedy or brief-detention safeguards, so it sits below that anchor's more operational protection.

Lower: that anchor documents inspectors, oversight discipline and prompt compensation in practice. Here implementation is explicitly inconsistent, reporting is low, and political hostility is documented, so working protection is not established.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: national constitutional and anti-discrimination protections plus hate-crime penalties apply uniformly, capital courts and NGOs provide litigable precedent and legal aid, but ministries refused precedential effect and March 2026 reporting stresses inconsistent implementation. No universal-exposure or organised targeting is documented; the operative risks are social/political hostility, under-reporting and unproven recourse, compounded by silence on border, facilities, custody and visitor care. That pattern supports Reduced Risk, below jurisdictions with demonstrated visitor-facing remedies.
